title: AT&T Partners With OpenAI For Legal Dept. Revamp
source_used: Artificial Lawyer (Law360 is behind a paywall; AT&T newsroom page returned 403)
key_facts: AT&T LegalEdge, the telecom company's new in-house legal group, is partnering with OpenAI to develop AI-enabled legal workflows.
LegalEdge launched in January 2026 and has handled nearly 100 matters in its first six months, per AT&T.
The aim is an AT&T Legal Department-wide capability to make knowledge and expertise more accessible, in the words of general counsel David McAtee, who adds that legal judgment remains human.

Jason Boehmig, OpenAI's general manager for the legal industry (previously co-founder of Ironclad), says they are exploring how AI can put institutional knowledge to work with lawyers' judgment at the centre.
The announcement came after OpenAI announced Astra for Law with legal-tech plugins.
Artificial Lawyer's own view: it may mean lower legal spend and less routine work going to outside law firms ("We shall see").
quote_evidence: AT&T LegalEdge, the telecom giant’s new inhouse legal agency, is partnering with OpenAI to develop AI-enabled legal workflows.
